newsitem.title: USA: FCC approval of Bell Atlantic deal expected soon.
newsitem.headline: FCC approval of Bell Atlantic deal expected soon.

text.p: The Federal Communications Commission is expected to act on Bell Atlantic Corp's planned $23 billion merger with NYNEX Corp this week, industry and government officials said.
"It's a foregone conclusion that it will be approved," analyst Jeffrey Kagan of Kagan Telecom Associates in Atlanta said Tuesday.
Approval represents the last hurdle to creation of the nation's No. 2 phone company, following long-distance giant AT&T Corp.
"When that (FCC approval) happens, don't expect a lot of change," Kagan said. "Real change will occur when the company feels the pinch of competition."

That competition, he noted, would come from long-distance carriers such as AT&T Corp, MCI Communications Corp and Sprint Corp entering the new Bell Atlantic's 13-state local calling market in the Northeast.

The FCC is expected to attach a number of conditions to the deal. They are designed to ensure the two Baby Bells open their phone market in the Northeast to rivals wanting to offer local phone service. The companies agreed to the provisions last month, paving the way for FCC approval.
The deal was first announced in April 1996. The new Bell Atlantic will serve an area stretching from Maine to Virginia that ecompasses 39 million phone lines.
